To find stationary points, take the first derivative of y=f(x), calling it f'(x). Set f'(x) equal to zero and solve for x. These x-values are candidates for stationary points. Then evaluate f(x) at these points to find corresponding y-values. These points are where the slope of the tangent is zero, indicating local maxima, minima, or points of inflection.
